title: Stopping OTP abuse before the SMS bill arrives
summary: Protect a login that sends paid SMS from scripts that send thousands of them.
context: Malleshwaram Mart logs people in with a one-time code by SMS. One weekend, a bot sent 400,000 codes to a block of premium-rate numbers, and the bill came to more than a month of infrastructure. The team found out from the invoice.
A real customer must still be able to log in quickly, including one who mistyped their number or whose code was slow to arrive.
must_handle: A single number, device or network cannot trigger unlimited messages.
A real person retrying a late code is not locked out.
A spike in sending is noticed within minutes, not at the end of the month.
Sending can be stopped by country or prefix in an emergency.
A code cannot be guessed by trying many times.
show_in_answer: Each limit, what it counts and where it sits.
What a real customer experiences when they hit one.
The signals you watch, and who gets told.
The fallback if the SMS provider goes down.
